1 潜在剖面分析(LPA)


Latent Profile Analysis (LPA) is a statistical method used to identify unobserved subgroups or latent classes within a population based on individuals’ responses to multiple observed variables. It is a type of mixture modeling, specifically suited for continuous data, and belongs to the broader family of latent variable models.


Key Concepts of LPA:

  • Latent Variables: These are variables that cannot be directly measured but are inferred from observed data. In LPA, latent variables represent the unobserved profiles or subgroups in the population that individuals belong to.

  • Latent Profiles/Classes: LPA aims to classify individuals into latent profiles, or subgroups, based on their response patterns across observed variables. Each latent profile is characterized by a distinct pattern of values across the observed indicators.

  • Observed Variables: These are the measured variables used in the analysis. In LPA, observed variables are typically continuous (e.g., psychological traits, behavioral scores, or survey responses).


Steps in LPA:

  • Selection of Observed Variables: Researchers choose a set of observed variables that are relevant to the research question and are assumed to be indicators of the latent profiles.

  • Model Specification: The number of latent profiles (i.e., the number of subgroups or clusters) is determined, often using model fit indices such as Akaike Information Criterion (AIC), Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC), and other criteria.

  • Model Estimation: LPA models are typically estimated using maximum likelihood estimation (MLE), which estimates the probability that each individual belongs to each latent profile.

  • Interpretation of Profiles: After identifying the latent profiles, researchers interpret each profile based on its mean or pattern of observed variables. This helps to characterize the distinct subgroups or patterns in the population.

  • Model Evaluation: The model’s fit and validity are assessed using various fit indices and potentially external validation (such as cross-validation or external datasets).

LPA-案例数据集:mtcars((mpg, hp, wt, qsec)

## 案例数据结构：数值型
## 'data.frame':    32 obs. of  4 variables:
##  $ mpg : num  21 21 22.8 21.4 18.7 18.1 14.3 24.4 22.8 19.2 ...
##  $ hp  : num  110 110 93 110 175 105 245 62 95 123 ...
##  $ wt  : num  2.62 2.88 2.32 3.21 3.44 ...
##  $ qsec: num  16.5 17 18.6 19.4 17 ...
